pensamiento:
I'm going through the user story checks one at a time: the role and action in QUS-001, a single objective in QUS-002, no notes in QUS-003, and QUS-004's benefit, which reads as a justification, so it passes. QUS-005 has no tech terms, and I'm now looking at QUS-006, where "draw" is ambiguous and "completed" is undefined.

I'm checking QUS-006 more closely: "draw" is ambiguous, and "completed" doesn't say when a draw is actually done. CTX-PP-034 gives a concrete end point, so the window is unclear here and I'm flagging it as a major defect. For QUS-007, the two sources define the closing moment differently, but they don't strictly contradict each other, so I'm treating it as a related question under QUS-006 rather than a separate blocking defect.

I'm weighing whether the deadline in CTX-PP-034 ("until the last person selects a card and all are shown") is the same as the "draw completed" in EV-16, since if they differ, the window is contradictory and needs the analyst to clarify. For QUS-008, the role and action overlap with CTX-PP-034 and the purpose is close, but the deadlines differ, so I'll treat it as an overlap to note rather than a separate defect.

I'm now deciding QUS-007 is a real contradiction rather than just a related question: EV-16 lets changes continue until the draw is completed, while CTX-PP-034 closes the window once the last person has selected a card and everything is shown. If those two end events differ, the same behaviour is governed by conflicting rules, so I'll mark it as a blocking defect and keep QUS-008 as compliant, with only its overlap noted.

I'm checking INV-001 and INV-002 next, and both pass since there's no dependency and the benefit is clear. For INV-003 the key gap is the closing condition for the change window, which the team can't estimate without, so I'm treating it as the same root cause as the QUS-006 defect rather than a separate one.

I'm settling on INV-003 as a defect too, since the missing closing rule is what the team would need to estimate it, and I'll treat that as the same gap as QUS-006. INV-004 looks small enough to estimate at 2 or 3 points, so it passes. INV-005 has no acceptance criteria, which makes it a blocking defect. For DOR-001, the change depends only on the internal draw mechanism and CTX-PP-034, with nothing external involved, so I'll mark it as not applicable.

I'm settling the defect list now: QUS-006, QUS-007, INV-003 and INV-005 are in, and DOR-002 is a second flag on the same missing window rule, so I'll keep it as its own item.

I'm settling INV-003 as a defect after all, since the missing closing rule is exactly what the team needs before it can estimate the change. For the estimate, the change itself is simple, so I'm going to call the estimation tool once rather than guess.

recomendaciones.texto: Definir qué significa 'draw has not been completed' (ronda completada). Hoy el término es ambiguo: indicar el evento exacto (p. ej., todas las estimaciones seleccionadas y reveladas) y usar el mismo término en toda la HU.

Resolver la contradicción con CTX-PP-034, que permite cambiar la estimación hasta que el último participante selecciona carta y todas se muestran. EV-16 usa 'ronda completada' como límite. Confirmar con producto cuál es la ventana vigente y alinear ambas HU.
Sin el evento de cierre de la ronda no se puede estimar con seguridad. Agregar la regla de cierre y, si aplica, qué ocurre al cambiar la estimación (p. ej., si se actualiza el resultado ya visible).

Agregar criterios de aceptación observables, por ejemplo: 'Mientras la ronda no esté completada, el participante puede cambiar su estimación y el valor nuevo reemplaza al anterior'; 'Al completarse la ronda, el participante ya no puede cambiar su estimación y se muestra un mensaje'.
Definir el caso de error: qué pasa si el participante intenta cambiar la estimación después de cerrada la ronda (bloqueo, mensaje, etc.) y si el cambio está limitado en número de veces, si aplica.
